gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured figure for any charger other than the UGREEN; the only alternative I found with a named test is Twelve South's 50 W PlugBug, where Cult of Mac saw at most 48 W to one device and a 29 W + 19 W split between an iPad Pro and an iPhone.
standout_why: Best Batteries (en.best-batteries.com, cited in the 2026-11-13 19:32 chat) already publishes the strongest measurements for the UGREEN Nexode 65W travel charger: about 62 W delivered to a laptop, 91.6% efficiency, a 45 W + 20 W split and 135 g. SmartGadgetKit (cited in the 2026-11-13 20:36 chat) repeats iMore's 45 W + 20 W split, and Windows Central's 'under an hour' recharges of a ROG Ally and a Surface Pro X. Android Central came through blank on fetch, without any product names or figures. MobilePlusTech says it did not use the products and gives only maker figures. The CNA and thisUSB fetches failed. So measured figures for the top pick are already on a cited rival page. My only new measured figure is for a 50 W charger that falls outside the 65 W question, so it is useful only as a footnote.
decides: This confirms the pick and does not change it. The UGREEN Nexode 65W travel charger is the only candidate with independent measurements: Best Batteries recorded about 62 W into a laptop and 91.6% efficiency. None of the alternatives ChatGPT offered (Native Union 67W, j5create JUP3565V/CV, KUXIU 65W UltraSlim, Verbatim 32201, D-Link DCP-651) has a published measurement I could find. The page can state honestly that 'the UGREEN is the only one here that a named tester has measured'. That supports it as the lowest-risk pick, but no rival will see it as news.

A temperature reading for any candidate: none published by a named tester. SmartGadgetKit says 'runs warm under a full load' without a figure; Best Batteries says it 'does not run excessively hot' without a figure.
